title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Carbon Set. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Carbon Set
options.lineage: multipart bills of lading, customs declarations and carbon-copy order sets
options.thesis: Sourcing is a document changing hands, so the interface is the set of copies, each party's sheet tinted and stamped, and it refuses the dashboard-of-cards arrangement this category always ships.
options.viewport: One ruled sheet fills the width, the brief typed into its head block, the twelve suppliers as numbered lines below, each carrying its clearance stamp or its strike-through with the reason typed beside it. The approve action sits in the foot block where a signature goes.
options.risk: Reads as pastiche when the stamps become decoration instead of live state.

raised.raise: Every measured value shows its distance from the limit, so a supplier drifting toward a ceiling is visible before it fails.
Tabular data sets at real density with no padding, so a full negotiation reads on one screen.

options.label: The Monograph
options.lineage: Certificates of Analysis and pharmacopoeia monographs
options.thesis: The lab report is the document a buyer already trusts, so the whole interface is set as one, with a specification column and a result column that never leave each other's side.
options.viewport: A two-column ruled table runs the page, specification on the left and measured result on the right, every failing row broken by a heavy rule with the deviation typed in the margin.
options.risk: It is where most runs in this category land, and it can read as a spreadsheet with better typography.

options.label: The Course Overlay
options.lineage: orienteering maps, ISOM ink standards and control descriptions
options.thesis: The specification is fixed terrain in a strict ink language, and each negotiation is a numbered course drawn over it that never edits the ground beneath.
options.viewport: A fixed field of specification bands fills the page, each supplier's negotiation drawn over it as a numbered purple leg, with a legend table ranking every symbol.
options.case: Holds product clarity outright: it separates what cannot change from what is being negotiated, which is the exact structure of this task. Loses audience identification, because a sourcing buyer does not read maps.
options.risk: The ink language needs teaching before it reads, and a buyer working in short bursts has no time for a legend.

options.label: Night Instrument Panel
options.lineage: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack
options.thesis: Six luminous gauges hold a buyer's trust while a run proceeds unseen.
options.viewport: Two ranked rows of three gauges, each owning one truth about the run.
options.case: Fuses poorly: twelve suppliers and four escalation kinds do not reduce to six dials, and the dark panel breaks Aonic's pinned off-white ground.
options.kept: Deviation shows before the alarm does.
options.risk: Gauges flatten the detail a buyer must read before approving.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda, dense barcode columns in pure black and white
options.thesis: Every offer is a column in one strobing data field.
options.viewport: A wall of hairline columns with tabular numbers packed into the margin.
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: pure black and white refuses Aonic's pinned palette, and a buyer approving a purchase needs named reasons.
options.kept: Density courage. Data sets at its real size with nothing padded.
options.risk: Beautiful and unreadable at the moment a decision is due.

options.label: Seedbed Lobes
options.lineage: saturated green ground with floating white capsule bars
options.thesis: The interface floats as detached lozenges over one owning colour.
options.viewport: A green field with a floating white nav capsule and an oversized flush-left headline.
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: it is consumer marketing dressing on an operational tool, and it carries no vocabulary for pass, fail or pending.
options.kept: Colour committed at page scale instead of scattered as accents.
options.risk: Nothing in it can express a failed heavy metal reading.

options.label: Deployable Sheet
options.lineage: a Miura-fold sheet opening from a hand-sized packet
options.thesis: One brief unfolds into the full field of offers.
options.viewport: A compact packet that deploys into a tessellated field of linked cells.
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: the fold is a transition, not a working surface, and a buyer returning mid-run needs the field already open.
options.kept: One control propagating a change across every linked cell.
options.risk: The metaphor costs a step on every visit and pays once.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.lineage: workers cutting blocks of weather from a cumulus cliff
options.thesis: Offers are cut, lifted and assembled as temporary blocks.
options.viewport: Stacked cloud blocks with deep blue gaps and measurements set in mono.
options.case: Fuses poorly on both axes: nothing in a surreal quarry maps to a laboratory limit or a price ceiling, and dissolution is the wrong promise for a purchase record.
options.kept: Sections read as cut volumes with real weight between them.
options.risk: It would have to be explained before it could be used.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The procurement dashboard every vendor ships, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A left nav rail, four summary tiles across the top and a sortable table below.
canonCard.risk: A reviewer has seen it a hundred times and will remember nothing about it.
